title: PSU vs WWU: tuition, size, location
summary: Portland State University (PSU) versus Western Washington University (WWU). Also searched as WWU vs PSU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Western Washington University (WWU) and Portland State University (PSU) are both public institutions, but they differ in several key aspects. WWU, located in Bellingham, has an undergraduate enrollment of 13,544 students, slightly higher than PSU's 13,182 students in Portland. Tuition for in-state students at WWU is $9,582, which is lower compared to PSU's in-state tuition of $11,679. These differences reflect variations in location, size, and cost between the two universities. Overall, WWU vs PSU offers prospective students distinct options depending on their preferences for city environment and tuition expenses.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance at Western Washington University (WWU) vs Portland State University (PSU), in-state tuition at WWU is $9,582, which is less expensive than PSU's in-state tuition of $11,679. For out-of-state students, WWU charges $28,707, while PSU's out-of-state tuition is slightly higher at $31,074. Regarding student debt, the median amount owed by graduates who completed their programs is $18,500 at WWU and $20,500 at PSU. These figures highlight that WWU generally offers a more affordable tuition rate and lower median debt compared to PSU, which may be important considerations for prospective students evaluating WWU vs PSU.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Western Washington University (WWU) and Portland State University (PSU) both provide diverse learning environments in urban settings but differ in campus location and undergraduate enrollment. WWU is situated in Bellingham, Washington, and enrolls 13,544 undergraduate students, while PSU is located in Portland, Oregon, with a slightly smaller undergraduate population of 13,182. These enrollment figures reflect the scale of each institution's campus community. The urban campuses of WWU vs PSU offer students access to city resources and opportunities, though the distinct regional contexts of Bellingham and Portland contribute to different campus experiences.

sections.heading: Accreditation
paragraphs: Western Washington University (WWU) and Portland State University (PSU) are both accredited public institutions, ensuring that they meet established standards of quality in higher education. Accreditation is a critical factor for students when evaluating WWU vs PSU, as it affects credit transferability, eligibility for federal financial aid, and recognition of degrees by employers and graduate programs. While specific accrediting bodies are not detailed here, both universities maintain accreditation status that supports their academic offerings and institutional integrity.

sections.heading: Pick WWU if
paragraphs: Pick Western Washington University (WWU) if you prefer a public institution with a high admission rate of approximately 93.25%, indicating a more accessible entry compared to more selective universities. WWU offers in-state tuition at $9,582, which is relatively affordable for residents. Additionally, the university has a completion rate of about 64.64% within 150% of the expected time, reflecting a solid proportion of students successfully finishing their programs. These factors make WWU a suitable choice for students seeking an accessible public university with reasonable tuition costs and a good likelihood of degree completion when considering WWU vs Portland State University (PSU).

sections.heading: Pick PSU if
paragraphs: Pick Portland State University (PSU) if you are looking for a public institution with a high admission rate of approximately 90.87%, which suggests a relatively accessible entry process. PSU's in-state tuition is $11,679, which is higher than some comparable institutions but may be justified by its urban location in Portland. The university has a completion rate of about 52.66% within 150% of the expected time, indicating that just over half of the students complete their programs within this timeframe. These factors make PSU a viable option for students prioritizing admission accessibility and willing to invest in a city-based public university when comparing Western Washington University (WWU) vs Portland State University (PSU).
